top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clock) rests on a distinct, reproduced invention: the magic-wavelength lattice cancels the trap light shift on the clock transition so many neutral atoms are interrogated at once, which neither the 2005 comb nor the 2012 ion-control prize contains, and it was confirmed with Sr, Yb and Hg at the 10^-18 level. Maturity is high and the two-name allocation maps onto two identifiable contributions, provided the citation stays narrow and does not adjudicate lattice versus ion clocks. P002 (magic-angle graphene) is a strong prediction-then-discovery case but is less mature, with the pairing mechanism unsettled and first author Yuan Cao outside the three names, so I rank it second, ahead of no award.
recusal_note: No conflict with Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer is apparent from my profile. My circuit-QED and WACQT ties would matter only for a circuit-QED or quantum-computing hardware proposal, and none is on this slate.
